sections.what: On start, creates the email sender if all four mail server settings are present, or warns and switches to fallback mode. The send method delivers the email when the sender exists, and otherwise prints the full message to the log.
sections.why: Lets the app send real email in production and still work in development.
sections.watch_out: The fallback log includes the full message body, so keep it out of production logs.

summary: Sends emails through an SMTP server when settings are present, and otherwise prints the email to the server log.
purpose: Delivers emails such as account messages or alerts.
why: Likely reason: lets developers run the app without an email server while still seeing what would be sent.
how: On start, it creates an email sender only when the host, port, user and password settings are all present. When asked to send, it uses the sender if available, otherwise writes the full email to the log. Send errors are logged and not raised.
inputs: Recipient address, subject, plain text body and optional HTML body, plus environment settings for the server and sender.
outputs: Nothing returned. Success or failure is written to the log.
risks: Without SMTP settings the full email text, which may contain codes or personal details, is written to the log. Failed sends are not retried or reported to the caller.
debug: If emails do not arrive, check the startup log for the missing setting warning and check the SMTP values. If a send fails, read the error logged with the recipient address.
